reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 describes elastic anisotropy evolution in NbTaTiV, not HfNbTaTiZr, and does not link it to dislocation activity or work hardening. E2 and E3 compare strength of HfNbTaTiZr with other alloys but provide no data on lattice distortion, thermal expansion, or work hardening/softening transitions in HfNbTaTiZr. The premises are largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Large atomic size mismatch in HfNbTaTiZr causes significant lattice distortions that evolve with temperature
Differential thermal expansion increases elastic anisotropy and local lattice strain up to ~800°C
Enhanced lattice strain at ~800°C activates additional dislocation slip systems and promotes work hardening
Above ~800°C, thermal expansion reduces lattice friction and weakens interatomic bonds, causing work softening
The alloy exhibits a transition from work hardening to work softening between ~800°C and 1000°C
